title: Login Now Checks Your Google ID Token, Not a Password | vitalii.no
description:
The only thing guarding Klient was a single shared password. Anyone who had it could log in — there was no way to tell which person was actually using the app, or to cut off just one of them without changing the password for everyone else.

server.mjs now adds a Google sign-in button. The browser sends Google's ID token to the server, which verifies it against Google — checking the audience claim and that the email itself is verified — and then checks that email against a comma-separated allow-list before it will set a session cookie. The old password login still works as a fallback for as long as that variable stays set, and logging out now clears both cookies at once.

Access now ties to a specific, verified Google account instead of one password everyone shares. Revoking one person is a one-line change — removing their email from the allow-list — instead of resetting a password every other user would also need again, and each session now lasts 30 days before it needs renewing.
